origin.description: Build a zoo from an atomic vector or array, using the row count as the index.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An atomic object. The index is seq_len(NROW(x)).
Further arguments passed to zoo. order.by cannot be one of them, because the index is already supplied.

origin.details: The method calls zoo(structure(x, dim = dim(x)), index(x), ...). index.default is the integer sequence 1 through the number of rows. Passing order.by as well is the error that a formal argument was matched by multiple actual arguments. frequency is forwarded, so a vector can still become a zooreg.
origin.example:
x <- as.zoo.default(c(4, 5))
cat(paste(coredata(x), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")
cat(paste(index(x), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")

translation.description: Build a zoo from an atomic vector or array, using the row count as the index.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A list or NumPy array. The index is 1 through the number of rows.

arguments.name: frequency
arguments.text: Observations per unit of time, forwarded to the zoo constructor.

arguments.name: calendar
arguments.text: When true, frequency 4 or 12 stores the index as yearqtr or yearmon.

translation.details: order_by is rejected. The index is the integer sequence 1..NROW before zoo applies frequency. A matrix keeps its shape and column-major order.
translation.example:
from zoo.as_zoo import as_zoo_default
import numpy as np
x = as_zoo_default([4, 5])
print(" ".join(str(int(v)) for v in np.asarray(x.data).reshape(-1)))
print(" ".join(str(int(v)) for v in np.asarray(x.index).reshape(-1)))
